//! A lexer for the supported subset of C.
//!
//! Produces a flat token stream with 1-based line numbers. Preprocessor
//! directives (lines starting with `#`, e.g. `#include`) are skipped, and
//! both `//` and `/* */` comments are stripped.

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum Tok {
    // Literals / identifiers
    Ident(String),
    Int(i64),
    Float(f64),
    Char(char),
    Str(String),

    // Keywords
    KwInt,
    KwChar,
    KwDouble,
    KwFloat,
    KwVoid,
    KwLong,
    KwIf,
    KwElse,
    KwWhile,
    KwFor,
    KwReturn,
    KwBreak,
    KwContinue,
    KwStruct,
    KwTypedef,
    KwSizeof,

    // Punctuation / operators
    LParen,
    RParen,
    LBrace,
    RBrace,
    LBracket,
    RBracket,
    Semicolon,
    Comma,
    Assign,     // =
    Plus,       // +
    Minus,      // -
    Star,       // *
    Slash,      // /
    Percent,    // %
    Amp,        // &
    PlusPlus,   // ++
    MinusMinus, // --
    PlusEq,     // +=
    MinusEq,    // -=
    StarEq,     // *=
    SlashEq,    // /=
    Eq,         // ==
    Ne,         // !=
    Lt,         // <
    Gt,         // >
    Le,         // <=
    Ge,         // >=
    AndAnd,     // &&
    OrOr,       // ||
    Not,        // !
    Arrow,      // ->
    Dot,        // .
    Question,   // ?
    Colon,      // :

    Eof,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Token {
    pub tok: Tok,
    pub line: usize,
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct LexError {
    pub message: String,
    pub line: usize,
}

pub fn lex(src: &str) -> Result<Vec<Token>, LexError> {
    let chars: Vec<char> = src.chars().collect();
    let mut i = 0usize;
    let mut line = 1usize;
    let mut out: Vec<Token> = Vec::new();

    let n = chars.len();
    while i < n {
        let c = chars[i];

        // Newlines
        if c == '\n' {
            line += 1;
            i += 1;
            continue;
        }
        // Whitespace
        if c.is_whitespace() {
            i += 1;
            continue;
        }
        // Preprocessor directive: skip to end of line.
        if c == '#' {
            while i < n && chars[i] != '\n' {
                i += 1;
            }
            continue;
        }
        // Comments
        if c == '/' && i + 1 < n && chars[i + 1] == '/' {
            while i < n && chars[i] != '\n' {
                i += 1;
            }
            continue;
        }
        if c == '/' && i + 1 < n && chars[i + 1] == '*' {
            i += 2;
            while i + 1 < n && !(chars[i] == '*' && chars[i + 1] == '/') {
                if chars[i] == '\n' {
                    line += 1;
                }
                i += 1;
            }
            i += 2; // consume */
            continue;
        }

        // Identifiers / keywords
        if c.is_alphabetic() || c == '_' {
            let start = i;
            while i < n && (chars[i].is_alphanumeric() || chars[i] == '_') {
                i += 1;
            }
            let word: String = chars[start..i].iter().collect();
            let tok = match word.as_str() {
                "int" => Tok::KwInt,
                "char" => Tok::KwChar,
                "double" => Tok::KwDouble,
                "float" => Tok::KwFloat,
                "void" => Tok::KwVoid,
                "long" => Tok::KwLong,
                "if" => Tok::KwIf,
                "else" => Tok::KwElse,
                "while" => Tok::KwWhile,
                "for" => Tok::KwFor,
                "return" => Tok::KwReturn,
                "break" => Tok::KwBreak,
                "continue" => Tok::KwContinue,
                "struct" => Tok::KwStruct,
                "typedef" => Tok::KwTypedef,
                "sizeof" => Tok::KwSizeof,
                _ => Tok::Ident(word),
            };
            out.push(Token { tok, line });
            continue;
        }

        // Numbers (int or float)
        if c.is_ascii_digit() {
            let start = i;
            let mut is_float = false;
            while i < n && (chars[i].is_ascii_digit() || chars[i] == '.') {
                if chars[i] == '.' {
                    is_float = true;
                }
                i += 1;
            }
            // Optional float suffix f/F
            if i < n && (chars[i] == 'f' || chars[i] == 'F') {
                is_float = true;
                i += 1;
            }
            let text: String = chars[start..i].iter().filter(|c| **c != 'f' && **c != 'F').collect();
            if is_float {
                let v: f64 = text.parse().map_err(|_| LexError {
                    message: format!("invalid float literal '{}'", text),
                    line,
                })?;
                out.push(Token { tok: Tok::Float(v), line });
            } else {
                let v: i64 = text.parse().map_err(|_| LexError {
                    message: format!("invalid integer literal '{}'", text),
                    line,
                })?;
                out.push(Token { tok: Tok::Int(v), line });
            }
            continue;
        }

        // Char literal
        if c == '\'' {
            i += 1;
            if i >= n {
                return Err(LexError { message: "unterminated char literal".into(), line });
            }
            let ch = if chars[i] == '\\' {
                i += 1;
                if i >= n {
                    return Err(LexError { message: "unterminated escape".into(), line });
                }
                let e = decode_escape(chars[i]);
                i += 1;
                e
            } else {
                let ch = chars[i];
                i += 1;
                ch
            };
            if i >= n || chars[i] != '\'' {
                return Err(LexError { message: "unterminated char literal".into(), line });
            }
            i += 1; // closing '
            out.push(Token { tok: Tok::Char(ch), line });
            continue;
        }

        // String literal
        if c == '"' {
            i += 1;
            let mut s = String::new();
            while i < n && chars[i] != '"' {
                if chars[i] == '\\' {
                    i += 1;
                    if i >= n {
                        return Err(LexError { message: "unterminated escape".into(), line });
                    }
                    s.push(decode_escape(chars[i]));
                    i += 1;
                } else {
                    if chars[i] == '\n' {
                        line += 1;
                    }
                    s.push(chars[i]);
                    i += 1;
                }
            }
            if i >= n {
                return Err(LexError { message: "unterminated string literal".into(), line });
            }
            i += 1; // closing "
            out.push(Token { tok: Tok::Str(s), line });
            continue;
        }

        // Operators / punctuation (two-char first)
        let two: Option<Tok> = if i + 1 < n {
            match (c, chars[i + 1]) {
                ('+', '+') => Some(Tok::PlusPlus),
                ('-', '-') => Some(Tok::MinusMinus),
                ('+', '=') => Some(Tok::PlusEq),
                ('-', '=') => Some(Tok::MinusEq),
                ('*', '=') => Some(Tok::StarEq),
                ('/', '=') => Some(Tok::SlashEq),
                ('=', '=') => Some(Tok::Eq),
                ('!', '=') => Some(Tok::Ne),
                ('<', '=') => Some(Tok::Le),
                ('>', '=') => Some(Tok::Ge),
                ('&', '&') => Some(Tok::AndAnd),
                ('|', '|') => Some(Tok::OrOr),
                ('-', '>') => Some(Tok::Arrow),
                _ => None,
            }
        } else {
            None
        };
        if let Some(tok) = two {
            out.push(Token { tok, line });
            i += 2;
            continue;
        }

        let one = match c {
            '(' => Tok::LParen,
            ')' => Tok::RParen,
            '{' => Tok::LBrace,
            '}' => Tok::RBrace,
            '[' => Tok::LBracket,
            ']' => Tok::RBracket,
            ';' => Tok::Semicolon,
            ',' => Tok::Comma,
            '=' => Tok::Assign,
            '+' => Tok::Plus,
            '-' => Tok::Minus,
            '*' => Tok::Star,
            '/' => Tok::Slash,
            '%' => Tok::Percent,
            '&' => Tok::Amp,
            '<' => Tok::Lt,
            '>' => Tok::Gt,
            '!' => Tok::Not,
            '.' => Tok::Dot,
            '?' => Tok::Question,
            ':' => Tok::Colon,
            other => {
                return Err(LexError {
                    message: format!("unexpected character '{}'", other),
                    line,
                })
            }
        };
        out.push(Token { tok: one, line });
        i += 1;
    }

    out.push(Token { tok: Tok::Eof, line });
    Ok(out)
}

fn decode_escape(c: char) -> char {
    match c {
        'n' => '\n',
        't' => '\t',
        'r' => '\r',
        '0' => '\0',
        '\\' => '\\',
        '\'' => '\'',
        '"' => '"',
        other => other,
    }
}

//! C language support: lex -> parse -> interpret -> ExecutionTrace.

pub mod ast;
pub mod interp;
pub mod lexer;
pub mod parser;

use crate::trace::ExecutionTrace;

/// A user-facing error from running C code, with an optional source line.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct CError {
    /// "lex" | "parse" | "runtime".
    pub stage: &'static str,
    pub message: String,
    pub line: Option<usize>,
    /// Machine-readable classification so the tutor can pick a hint sequence
    /// without re-parsing the human message. See `classify_runtime`.
    pub kind: &'static str,
}

/// Classify a lexer error message into a stable `kind` the tutor keys on.
fn classify_lex(message: &str) -> &'static str {
    if message.contains("unexpected character") {
        "lex_unexpected_char"
    } else if message.contains("unterminated string") {
        "lex_unterminated_string"
    } else if message.contains("unterminated char") || message.contains("unterminated escape") {
        "lex_unterminated_char"
    } else if message.contains("invalid integer") || message.contains("invalid float") {
        "lex_invalid_number"
    } else {
        "lex_error"
    }
}

/// Classify a parser error message into a stable `kind` the tutor keys on.
/// The parser's messages are stable, so substring matching is reliable.
fn classify_parse(message: &str) -> &'static str {
    // Specific "expected X, found Y" cases first.
    if message.contains("expected Semicolon") {
        "parse_missing_semicolon"
    } else if message.contains("expected RParen") {
        "parse_missing_rparen"
    } else if message.contains("expected LParen") {
        "parse_missing_lparen"
    } else if message.contains("expected RBrace") {
        "parse_missing_rbrace"
    } else if message.contains("expected LBrace") {
        "parse_missing_lbrace"
    } else if message.contains("expected RBracket") {
        "parse_missing_rbracket"
    } else if message.contains("expected identifier") {
        "parse_expected_identifier"
    } else if message.contains("expected a type") {
        "parse_expected_type"
    } else if message.contains("unexpected token in expression") {
        "parse_unexpected_in_expr"
    } else {
        "parse_error"
    }
}

/// Classify a runtime error message into a stable `kind` the tutor keys on.
/// Messages are produced by the interpreter and are stable, so matching on
/// substrings here is reliable.
fn classify_runtime(message: &str) -> &'static str {
    if message.contains("out of bounds") {
        "index_out_of_bounds"
    } else if message.contains("negative array index") {
        "negative_index"
    } else if message.contains("division by zero") {
        "division_by_zero"
    } else if message.contains("modulo by zero") {
        "modulo_by_zero"
    } else if message.contains("null pointer") {
        "null_deref"
    } else if message.contains("null/invalid pointer") {
        "null_deref"
    } else if message.contains("undeclared variable") {
        "undeclared_variable"
    } else if message.contains("unknown function") {
        "unknown_function"
    } else if message.contains("recursion too deep")
        || message.contains("call stack overflow")
    {
        "stack_overflow"
    } else if message.contains("infinite loop") || message.contains("step limit") {
        "infinite_loop"
    } else if message.contains("no 'main'") {
        "no_main"
    } else {
        "runtime_other"
    }
}

/// Lex, parse, and interpret a C program, producing an execution trace.
pub fn run(source: &str) -> Result<ExecutionTrace, CError> {
    let tokens = lexer::lex(source).map_err(|e| CError {
        stage: "lex",
        kind: classify_lex(&e.message),
        message: e.message,
        line: Some(e.line),
    })?;

    let mut parser = parser::Parser::new(tokens);
    let program = parser.parse_program().map_err(|e| CError {
        stage: "parse",
        kind: classify_parse(&e.message),
        message: e.message,
        line: Some(e.line),
    })?;

    let interp = interp::Interp::new(&program);
    interp.run().map_err(|e| CError {
        stage: "runtime",
        kind: classify_runtime(&e.message),
        message: e.message,
        line: if e.line == 0 { None } else { Some(e.line) },
    })
}

//! CodeTutor backend HTTP server.
//!
//! Exposes `POST /api/run` which takes `{ language, code }` and returns an
//! execution trace for the visualizer (or structured errors for the alert
//! panel). Only C is implemented here; other languages are handled by
//! teammates and currently return a "not implemented" response.

mod c;
mod trace;

use axum::{
    extract::Json,
    http::StatusCode,
    response::IntoResponse,
    routing::{get, post},
    Router,
};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use tower_http::cors::{Any, CorsLayer};

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
struct RunRequest {
    language: String,
    code: String,
}

/// A problem surfaced to the frontend AlertPanel.
#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
struct ApiError {
    severity: String,
    message: String,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    line: Option<usize>,
    stage: String,
    /// Machine-readable classification the tutor uses to pick a hint sequence.
    kind: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
#[serde(untagged)]
enum RunResponse {
    Ok {
        ok: bool,
        trace: trace::ExecutionTrace,
    },
    Err {
        ok: bool,
        errors: Vec<ApiError>,
    },
}

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let cors = CorsLayer::new()
        .allow_origin(Any)
        .allow_methods(Any)
        .allow_headers(Any);

    let app = Router::new()
        .route("/api/health", get(health))
        .route("/api/run", post(run_handler))
        .layer(cors);

    let addr = "127.0.0.1:8080";
    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(addr)
        .await
        .expect("failed to bind address");
    println!("CodeTutor backend listening on http://{addr}");
    axum::serve(listener, app)
        .await
        .expect("server error");
}

async fn health() -> &'static str {
    "ok"
}

async fn run_handler(Json(req): Json<RunRequest>) -> impl IntoResponse {
    match req.language.as_str() {
        "c" => match c::run(&req.code) {
            Ok(trace) => (
                StatusCode::OK,
                Json(RunResponse::Ok { ok: true, trace }),
            ),
            Err(err) => (
                StatusCode::OK,
                Json(RunResponse::Err {
                    ok: false,
                    errors: vec![ApiError {
                        severity: "error".into(),
                        message: err.message,
                        line: err.line,
                        stage: err.stage.into(),
                        kind: err.kind.into(),
                    }],
                }),
            ),
        },
        other => (
            StatusCode::OK,
            Json(RunResponse::Err {
                ok: false,
                errors: vec![ApiError {
                    severity: "info".into(),
                    message: format!(
                        "language '{}' is not implemented in this backend yet",
                        other
                    ),
                    line: None,
                    stage: "dispatch".into(),
                    kind: "unsupported_language".into(),
                }],
            }),
        ),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn run_c(src: &str) -> trace::ExecutionTrace {
        c::run(src).expect("program should run")
    }

    #[test]
    fn runs_simple_loop_and_array() {
        let src = r#"
            int main(void) {
                int values[3] = {4, 5, 6};
                int sum = 0;
                for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
                    sum += values[i];
                }
                return sum;
            }
        "#;
        let trace = run_c(src);
        assert!(!trace.states.is_empty());
        // The final state should have a frame with sum = 15.
        let last = trace.states.last().unwrap();
        let main_frame = last.stack.last().unwrap();
        let sum = main_frame
            .variables
            .iter()
            .find(|v| v.name == "sum")
            .expect("sum var present");
        if let trace::Value::Primitive { display, .. } = &sum.value {
            assert_eq!(display, "15");
        } else {
            panic!("sum should be a primitive");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn pointer_and_deref() {
        let src = r#"
            int main(void) {
                int x = 7;
                int* p = &x;
                *p = 42;
                return x;
            }
        "#;
        let trace = run_c(src);
        let last = trace.states.last().unwrap();
        let main_frame = last.stack.last().unwrap();
        let x = main_frame.variables.iter().find(|v| v.name == "x").unwrap();
        if let trace::Value::Primitive { display, .. } = &x.value {
            assert_eq!(display, "42");
        } else {
            panic!("x should be a primitive");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn reports_division_by_zero() {
        let src = r#"
            int main(void) {
                int a = 1;
                int b = 0;
                int c = a / b;
                return c;
            }
        "#;
        let err = c::run(src).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(err.stage, "runtime");
        assert_eq!(err.kind, "division_by_zero");
        assert!(err.message.contains("division by zero"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn classifies_index_out_of_bounds() {
        let src = r#"
            int main(void) {
                int a[3] = {1, 2, 3};
                int y = a[5];
                return y;
            }
        "#;
        let err = c::run(src).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(err.stage, "runtime");
        assert_eq!(err.kind, "index_out_of_bounds");
    }

    #[test]
    fn classifies_null_deref() {
        let src = r#"
            int main(void) {
                int* p = 0;
                int y = *p;
                return y;
            }
        "#;
        let err = c::run(src).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(err.kind, "null_deref");
    }

    #[test]
    fn classifies_missing_semicolon() {
        // `int x = 5` with no semicolon before `return`.
        let src = "int main(void) { int x = 5 return 0; }";
        let err = c::run(src).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(err.stage, "parse");
        assert_eq!(err.kind, "parse_missing_semicolon");
    }

    #[test]
    fn classifies_unexpected_char() {
        let src = "int main(void) { int x = @; return 0; }";
        let err = c::run(src).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(err.stage, "lex");
        assert_eq!(err.kind, "lex_unexpected_char");
    }

    const BST_SRC: &str = r#"
        #include <stdio.h>
        #include <stdlib.h>

        typedef struct Node {
            int value;
            struct Node *left;
            struct Node *right;
        } Node;

        Node *insert(Node *root, int value) {
            if (root == NULL) {
                Node *node = malloc(sizeof *node);
                node->value = value;
                node->left = NULL;
                node->right = NULL;
                return node;
            }
            if (value < root->value) {
                root->left = insert(root->left, value);
            } else if (value > root->value) {
                root->right = insert(root->right, value);
            }
            return root;
        }

        void inorder(Node *root) {
            if (root == NULL) return;
            inorder(root->left);
            printf("%d ", root->value);
            inorder(root->right);
        }

        int main(void) {
            Node *root = NULL;
            int values[] = {8, 3, 10, 1, 6};
            int count = 5;
            for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
                root = insert(root, values[i]);
            }
            printf("Sorted: ");
            inorder(root);
            printf("\n");
            return 0;
        }
    "#;

    #[test]
    fn bst_builds_linked_node_structs() {
        let trace = run_c(BST_SRC);
        assert!(!trace.states.is_empty());
        let last = trace.states.last().unwrap();

        // At least one heap object is a Node struct.
        let node_structs: Vec<_> = last
            .heap
            .values()
            .filter_map(|o| match o {
                trace::HeapObject::Struct { type_name, fields, .. } if type_name == "Node" => {
                    Some(fields)
                }
                _ => None,
            })
            .collect();
        assert!(
            !node_structs.is_empty(),
            "expected at least one Node struct in the heap"
        );

        // At least one Node has a pointer field that references another heap
        // object (proving node->node linkage).
        let has_link = node_structs.iter().any(|fields| {
            fields.iter().any(|f| {
                matches!(
                    &f.value,
                    trace::Value::Ref {
                        target: Some(trace::RefTarget::Heap { .. })
                    }
                )
            })
        });
        assert!(has_link, "expected a Node with a pointer field linking to another node");
    }

    #[test]
    fn ternary_evaluates_true_branch() {
        let src = r#"
            int main(void) {
                int x = (1 < 2) ? 10 : 20;
                return x;
            }
        "#;
        let trace = run_c(src);
        let last = trace.states.last().unwrap();
        let main_frame = last.stack.last().unwrap();
        let x = main_frame.variables.iter().find(|v| v.name == "x").unwrap();
        if let trace::Value::Primitive { display, .. } = &x.value {
            assert_eq!(display, "10");
        } else {
            panic!("x should be a primitive");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn null_check_and_struct_field_roundtrip() {
        let src = r#"
            typedef struct Node {
                int value;
                struct Node *next;
            } Node;

            int main(void) {
                Node *p = NULL;
                int wasNull = (p == NULL) ? 1 : 0;
                p = malloc(sizeof *p);
                p->value = 42;
                p->next = NULL;
                int v = p->value;
                int notNull = (p != NULL) ? 1 : 0;
                return v;
            }
        "#;
        let trace = run_c(src);
        let last = trace.states.last().unwrap();
        let main_frame = last.stack.last().unwrap();

        let was_null = main_frame.variables.iter().find(|v| v.name == "wasNull").unwrap();
        if let trace::Value::Primitive { display, .. } = &was_null.value {
            assert_eq!(display, "1", "p == NULL should be true when p is NULL");
        } else {
            panic!("wasNull should be a primitive");
        }

        let not_null = main_frame.variables.iter().find(|v| v.name == "notNull").unwrap();
        if let trace::Value::Primitive { display, .. } = &not_null.value {
            assert_eq!(display, "1", "p != NULL should be true after malloc");
        }

        let v = main_frame.variables.iter().find(|v| v.name == "v").unwrap();
        if let trace::Value::Primitive { display, .. } = &v.value {
            assert_eq!(display, "42", "struct field written then read back");
        } else {
            panic!("v should be a primitive");
        }
    }
}

//! AST for the supported subset of C.

/// A declared/base type. Pointers are tracked by `pointer_depth`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum BaseType {
    Int,
    Char,
    Double,
    Float,
    Long,
    Void,
    /// A user-defined struct type, carrying the canonical struct name.
    Struct(String),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct CType {
    pub base: BaseType,
    /// Number of `*` levels (0 = plain value, 1 = `int*`, etc.).
    pub pointer_depth: u32,
}

impl CType {
    pub fn display(&self) -> String {
        let base = match &self.base {
            BaseType::Int => "int".to_string(),
            BaseType::Char => "char".to_string(),
            BaseType::Double => "double".to_string(),
            BaseType::Float => "float".to_string(),
            BaseType::Long => "long".to_string(),
            BaseType::Void => "void".to_string(),
            BaseType::Struct(name) => format!("struct {}", name),
        };
        format!("{}{}", base, "*".repeat(self.pointer_depth as usize))
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum BinOp {
    Add,
    Sub,
    Mul,
    Div,
    Mod,
    Eq,
    Ne,
    Lt,
    Gt,
    Le,
    Ge,
    And,
    Or,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum UnOp {
    Neg,
    Not,
    /// Address-of: &x
    AddrOf,
    /// Dereference: *p
    Deref,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Expr {
    IntLit(i64),
    FloatLit(f64),
    CharLit(char),
    StrLit(String),
    Ident(String),
    /// Array indexing: base[index]
    Index(Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>),
    /// Unary operation.
    Unary(UnOp, Box<Expr>),
    /// Binary operation.
    Binary(BinOp, Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>),
    /// Assignment: target = value. Target is an lvalue expression.
    Assign(Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>),
    /// Function call: name(args...).
    Call(String, Vec<Expr>),
    /// Pre/post increment/decrement; bool = is_prefix, i64 = +1/-1.
    IncDec { target: Box<Expr>, delta: i64, prefix: bool },
    /// Ternary conditional: cond ? then_expr : else_expr.
    Ternary {
        cond: Box<Expr>,
        then_expr: Box<Expr>,
        else_expr: Box<Expr>,
    },
    /// Struct member access: base.field or base->field (arrow = true for ->).
    Member {
        base: Box<Expr>,
        field: String,
        arrow: bool,
    },
    /// sizeof operator. We don't model real bytes; instead we use synthetic
    /// units where a scalar/pointer is 1 unit and an array is `length` units.
    /// This makes the common `sizeof arr / sizeof arr[0]` idiom yield the
    /// array's length. `None` operand = sizeof(type), which is 1 unit.
    Sizeof(Option<Box<Expr>>),
    /// Null pointer literal (NULL).
    Null,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Stmt {
    /// Variable declaration, optionally with an initializer.
    /// For arrays, `array_len` is Some(n).
    VarDecl {
        ty: CType,
        name: String,
        array_len: Option<usize>,
        init: Option<Expr>,
        /// For `int a[] = {1,2,3}` or `int a[3] = {...}`.
        array_init: Option<Vec<Expr>>,
        line: usize,
    },
    ExprStmt(Expr, usize),
    If {
        cond: Expr,
        then_branch: Vec<Stmt>,
        else_branch: Option<Vec<Stmt>>,
        line: usize,
    },
    While {
        cond: Expr,
        body: Vec<Stmt>,
        line: usize,
    },
    For {
        init: Option<Box<Stmt>>,
        cond: Option<Expr>,
        step: Option<Expr>,
        body: Vec<Stmt>,
        line: usize,
    },
    Return(Option<Expr>, usize),
    Break(usize),
    Continue(usize),
    Block(Vec<Stmt>),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Param {
    pub ty: CType,
    pub name: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Function {
    /// Return type (kept for future type checking / coercion of return values).
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub ret: CType,
    pub name: String,
    pub params: Vec<Param>,
    pub body: Vec<Stmt>,
}

/// A struct type definition: `struct Name { CType field; ... }`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct StructDef {
    /// The canonical struct name (the tag after `struct`, or the typedef alias
    /// when there is no tag).
    pub name: String,
    pub fields: Vec<(CType, String)>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Program {
    pub functions: Vec<Function>,
    pub structs: Vec<StructDef>,
}

//! Recursive-descent parser for the supported subset of C.

use std::collections::HashSet;

use super::ast::*;
use super::lexer::{Tok, Token};

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ParseError {
    pub message: String,
    pub line: usize,
}

pub struct Parser {
    toks: Vec<Token>,
    pos: usize,
    /// Names (struct tags + typedef aliases) known to name a struct type.
    type_names: HashSet<String>,
}

type PResult<T> = Result<T, ParseError>;

impl Parser {
    pub fn new(toks: Vec<Token>) -> Self {
        let type_names = Self::collect_type_names(&toks);
        Parser { toks, pos: 0, type_names }
    }

    /// Pre-pass over the token stream to collect every identifier that names a
    /// struct type (the tag after `struct Name`, and any typedef alias). This
    /// lets `parse_type` recognize struct type names wherever they appear,
    /// regardless of definition order.
    fn collect_type_names(toks: &[Token]) -> HashSet<String> {
        let mut names = HashSet::new();
        let n = toks.len();
        let mut i = 0;
        while i < n {
            // `struct Name` -> Name is a type.
            if toks[i].tok == Tok::KwStruct {
                if let Tok::Ident(name) = &toks[i + 1.min(n - 1 - i)].tok {
                    names.insert(name.clone());
                }
            }
            // `typedef struct [Name] { ... } Alias;` -> Alias is a type.
            if toks[i].tok == Tok::KwTypedef {
                // Walk to the matching close brace, then the next ident before ';'.
                let mut j = i + 1;
                // skip to '{'
                while j < n && toks[j].tok != Tok::LBrace && toks[j].tok != Tok::Semicolon {
                    j += 1;
                }
                if j < n && toks[j].tok == Tok::LBrace {
                    let mut depth = 0;
                    while j < n {
                        match toks[j].tok {
                            Tok::LBrace => depth += 1,
                            Tok::RBrace => {
                                depth -= 1;
                                if depth == 0 {
                                    j += 1;
                                    break;
                                }
                            }
                            _ => {}
                        }
                        j += 1;
                    }
                    if j < n {
                        if let Tok::Ident(alias) = &toks[j].tok {
                            names.insert(alias.clone());
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            i += 1;
        }
        names
    }

    pub fn parse_program(&mut self) -> PResult<Program> {
        let mut functions = Vec::new();
        let mut structs = Vec::new();
        while !self.check(&Tok::Eof) {
            match self.peek() {
                Tok::KwTypedef => {
                    let defs = self.parse_typedef()?;
                    structs.extend(defs);
                }
                Tok::KwStruct => {
                    // Could be a struct definition `struct Name { ... };` or a
                    // function/decl using a struct type like `struct Node *f(...)`.
                    if self.is_struct_definition() {
                        structs.push(self.parse_struct_def()?);
                    } else {
                        functions.push(self.parse_function()?);
                    }
                }
                _ => functions.push(self.parse_function()?),
            }
        }
        Ok(Program { functions, structs })
    }

    /// Returns true if the upcoming tokens are `struct Name { ... };`
    /// (a definition) rather than `struct Name * foo(...)` (a declaration/fn).
    fn is_struct_definition(&self) -> bool {
        // peek: KwStruct Ident LBrace ...
        self.peek() == &Tok::KwStruct
            && matches!(self.peek_at(1), Tok::Ident(_))
            && self.peek_at(2) == &Tok::LBrace
    }

    /// Parse the field list between `{` and `}` of a struct body. Assumes the
    /// opening `{` has NOT yet been consumed.
    fn parse_struct_body(&mut self) -> PResult<Vec<(CType, String)>> {
        self.eat(&Tok::LBrace)?;
        let mut fields = Vec::new();
        while !self.check(&Tok::RBrace) && !self.check(&Tok::Eof) {
            let ty = self.parse_type()?;
            let name = self.expect_ident()?;
            self.eat(&Tok::Semicolon)?;
            fields.push((ty, name));
        }
        self.eat(&Tok::RBrace)?;
        Ok(fields)
    }

    /// Parse `struct Name { fields };`.
    fn parse_struct_def(&mut self) -> PResult<StructDef> {
        self.eat(&Tok::KwStruct)?;
        let name = self.expect_ident()?;
        self.type_names.insert(name.clone());
        let fields = self.parse_struct_body()?;
        self.eat(&Tok::Semicolon)?;
        Ok(StructDef { name, fields })
    }

    /// Parse `typedef struct [Tag] { fields } Alias;`. Registers both the tag
    /// (if present) and the alias as names for the same struct, returning a
    /// StructDef for each so lookups by either name succeed.
    fn parse_typedef(&mut self) -> PResult<Vec<StructDef>> {
        self.eat(&Tok::KwTypedef)?;
        self.eat(&Tok::KwStruct)?;
        // Optional struct tag.
        let tag = if let Tok::Ident(name) = self.peek().clone() {
            self.advance();
            Some(name)
        } else {
            None
        };
        let fields = self.parse_struct_body()?;
        let alias = self.expect_ident()?;
        self.eat(&Tok::Semicolon)?;

        self.type_names.insert(alias.clone());
        if let Some(t) = &tag {
            self.type_names.insert(t.clone());
        }

        // Canonical name: prefer the tag so `struct Node` and alias `Node`
        // resolve to the same definition.
        let canonical = tag.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| alias.clone());
        let mut defs = vec![StructDef { name: canonical.clone(), fields: fields.clone() }];
        if alias != canonical {
            defs.push(StructDef { name: alias, fields });
        }
        Ok(defs)
    }

    // ---- token helpers ----------------------------------------------------

    fn peek(&self) -> &Tok {
        &self.toks[self.pos].tok
    }

    fn peek_at(&self, offset: usize) -> &Tok {
        let idx = (self.pos + offset).min(self.toks.len() - 1);
        &self.toks[idx].tok
    }

    fn line(&self) -> usize {
        self.toks[self.pos].line
    }

    fn check(&self, t: &Tok) -> bool {
        self.peek() == t
    }

    fn advance(&mut self) -> Tok {
        let t = self.toks[self.pos].tok.clone();
        if self.pos < self.toks.len() - 1 {
            self.pos += 1;
        }
        t
    }

    fn eat(&mut self, t: &Tok) -> PResult<()> {
        if self.check(t) {
            self.advance();
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(ParseError {
                message: format!("expected {:?}, found {:?}", t, self.peek()),
                line: self.line(),
            })
        }
    }

    fn match_tok(&mut self, t: &Tok) -> bool {
        if self.check(t) {
            self.advance();
            true
        } else {
            false
        }
    }

    // ---- types ------------------------------------------------------------

    fn is_type_start(&self) -> bool {
        match self.peek() {
            Tok::KwInt
            | Tok::KwChar
            | Tok::KwDouble
            | Tok::KwFloat
            | Tok::KwVoid
            | Tok::KwLong
            | Tok::KwStruct => true,
            // A known struct type name, or `size_t`.
            Tok::Ident(name) => name == "size_t" || self.type_names.contains(name),
            _ => false,
        }
    }

    fn parse_type(&mut self) -> PResult<CType> {
        let base = match self.peek().clone() {
            Tok::KwInt => {
                self.advance();
                BaseType::Int
            }
            Tok::KwChar => {
                self.advance();
                BaseType::Char
            }
            Tok::KwDouble => {
                self.advance();
                BaseType::Double
            }
            Tok::KwFloat => {
                self.advance();
                BaseType::Float
            }
            Tok::KwLong => {
                self.advance();
                BaseType::Long
            }
            Tok::KwVoid => {
                self.advance();
                BaseType::Void
            }
            Tok::KwStruct => {
                self.advance();
                let name = self.expect_ident()?;
                BaseType::Struct(name)
            }
            Tok::Ident(name) if name == "size_t" => {
                self.advance();
                // Model size_t as a plain integer.
                BaseType::Long
            }
            Tok::Ident(name) if self.type_names.contains(&name) => {
                self.advance();
                BaseType::Struct(name)
            }
            other => {
                return Err(ParseError {
                    message: format!("expected a type, found {:?}", other),
                    line: self.line(),
                })
            }
        };
        let mut pointer_depth = 0;
        while self.match_tok(&Tok::Star) {
            pointer_depth += 1;
        }
        Ok(CType { base, pointer_depth })
    }

    fn expect_ident(&mut self) -> PResult<String> {
        match self.advance() {
            Tok::Ident(name) => Ok(name),
            other => Err(ParseError {
                message: format!("expected identifier, found {:?}", other),
                line: self.line(),
            }),
        }
    }

    // ---- functions --------------------------------------------------------

    fn parse_function(&mut self) -> PResult<Function> {
        let ret = self.parse_type()?;
        let name = self.expect_ident()?;
        self.eat(&Tok::LParen)?;
        let mut params = Vec::new();
        if !self.check(&Tok::RParen) {
            // Handle `void` param list.
            if self.check(&Tok::KwVoid) && self.peek_at(1) == &Tok::RParen {
                self.advance();
            } else {
                loop {
                    let ty = self.parse_type()?;
                    let pname = self.expect_ident()?;
                    params.push(Param { ty, name: pname });
                    if !self.match_tok(&Tok::Comma) {
                        break;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        self.eat(&Tok::RParen)?;
        self.eat(&Tok::LBrace)?;
        let body = self.parse_block_body()?;
        Ok(Function { ret, name, params, body })
    }

    /// Parse statements until a closing brace (which is consumed).
    fn parse_block_body(&mut self) -> PResult<Vec<Stmt>> {
        let mut stmts = Vec::new();
        while !self.check(&Tok::RBrace) && !self.check(&Tok::Eof) {
            stmts.push(self.parse_stmt()?);
        }
        self.eat(&Tok::RBrace)?;
        Ok(stmts)
    }

    // ---- statements -------------------------------------------------------

    fn parse_stmt(&mut self) -> PResult<Stmt> {
        let line = self.line();
        match self.peek() {
            Tok::LBrace => {
                self.advance();
                Ok(Stmt::Block(self.parse_block_body()?))
            }
            Tok::KwIf => self.parse_if(),
            Tok::KwWhile => self.parse_while(),
            Tok::KwFor => self.parse_for(),
            Tok::KwReturn => {
                self.advance();
                let expr = if self.check(&Tok::Semicolon) {
                    None
                } else {
                    Some(self.parse_expr()?)
                };
                self.eat(&Tok::Semicolon)?;
                Ok(Stmt::Return(expr, line))
            }
            Tok::KwBreak => {
                self.advance();
                self.eat(&Tok::Semicolon)?;
                Ok(Stmt::Break(line))
            }
            Tok::KwContinue => {
                self.advance();
                self.eat(&Tok::Semicolon)?;
                Ok(Stmt::Continue(line))
            }
            _ if self.is_type_start() => self.parse_var_decl(),
            _ => {
                let expr = self.parse_expr()?;
                self.eat(&Tok::Semicolon)?;
                Ok(Stmt::ExprStmt(expr, line))
            }
        }
    }

    fn parse_var_decl(&mut self) -> PResult<Stmt> {
        let line = self.line();
        let ty = self.parse_type()?;
        let name = self.expect_ident()?;

        // Array declaration: name[len]
        let mut array_len = None;
        if self.match_tok(&Tok::LBracket) {
            if let Tok::Int(n) = self.peek().clone() {
                self.advance();
                array_len = Some(n as usize);
            } else {
                array_len = Some(0); // size inferred from initializer
            }
            self.eat(&Tok::RBracket)?;
        }

        let mut init = None;
        let mut array_init = None;
        if self.match_tok(&Tok::Assign) {
            if self.check(&Tok::LBrace) {
                // Array initializer list { a, b, c }
                self.advance();
                let mut elems = Vec::new();
                if !self.check(&Tok::RBrace) {
                    loop {
                        elems.push(self.parse_expr()?);
                        if !self.match_tok(&Tok::Comma) {
                            break;
                        }
                        if self.check(&Tok::RBrace) {
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                }
                self.eat(&Tok::RBrace)?;
                if array_len.is_none() {
                    array_len = Some(elems.len());
                }
                array_init = Some(elems);
            } else {
                init = Some(self.parse_expr()?);
            }
        }
        self.eat(&Tok::Semicolon)?;
        Ok(Stmt::VarDecl {
            ty,
            name,
            array_len,
            init,
            array_init,
            line,
        })
    }

    fn parse_if(&mut self) -> PResult<Stmt> {
        let line = self.line();
        self.eat(&Tok::KwIf)?;
        self.eat(&Tok::LParen)?;
        let cond = self.parse_expr()?;
        self.eat(&Tok::RParen)?;
        let then_branch = self.parse_stmt_as_block()?;
        let else_branch = if self.match_tok(&Tok::KwElse) {
            Some(self.parse_stmt_as_block()?)
        } else {
            None
        };
        Ok(Stmt::If { cond, then_branch, else_branch, line })
    }

    fn parse_while(&mut self) -> PResult<Stmt> {
        let line = self.line();
        self.eat(&Tok::KwWhile)?;
        self.eat(&Tok::LParen)?;
        let cond = self.parse_expr()?;
        self.eat(&Tok::RParen)?;
        let body = self.parse_stmt_as_block()?;
        Ok(Stmt::While { cond, body, line })
    }

    fn parse_for(&mut self) -> PResult<Stmt> {
        let line = self.line();
        self.eat(&Tok::KwFor)?;
        self.eat(&Tok::LParen)?;

        let init = if self.check(&Tok::Semicolon) {
            self.advance();
            None
        } else if self.is_type_start() {
            Some(Box::new(self.parse_var_decl()?))
        } else {
            let e = self.parse_expr()?;
            self.eat(&Tok::Semicolon)?;
            Some(Box::new(Stmt::ExprStmt(e, line)))
        };

        let cond = if self.check(&Tok::Semicolon) {
            None
        } else {
            Some(self.parse_expr()?)
        };
        self.eat(&Tok::Semicolon)?;

        let step = if self.check(&Tok::RParen) {
            None
        } else {
            Some(self.parse_expr()?)
        };
        self.eat(&Tok::RParen)?;

        let body = self.parse_stmt_as_block()?;
        Ok(Stmt::For { init, cond, step, body, line })
    }

    /// Parse a single statement, wrapping a non-block as a one-element block.
    fn parse_stmt_as_block(&mut self) -> PResult<Vec<Stmt>> {
        if self.check(&Tok::LBrace) {
            self.advance();
            self.parse_block_body()
        } else {
            Ok(vec![self.parse_stmt()?])
        }
    }

    // ---- expressions (precedence climbing) --------------------------------

    fn parse_expr(&mut self) -> PResult<Expr> {
        self.parse_assignment()
    }

    fn parse_assignment(&mut self) -> PResult<Expr> {
        let left = self.parse_ternary()?;
        match self.peek() {
            Tok::Assign => {
                self.advance();
                let right = self.parse_assignment()?;
                Ok(Expr::Assign(Box::new(left), Box::new(right)))
            }
            Tok::PlusEq | Tok::MinusEq | Tok::StarEq | Tok::SlashEq => {
                let op = match self.advance() {
                    Tok::PlusEq => BinOp::Add,
                    Tok::MinusEq => BinOp::Sub,
                    Tok::StarEq => BinOp::Mul,
                    Tok::SlashEq => BinOp::Div,
                    _ => unreachable!(),
                };
                let right = self.parse_assignment()?;
                // a += b  =>  a = a + b
                let combined = Expr::Binary(op, Box::new(left.clone()), Box::new(right));
                Ok(Expr::Assign(Box::new(left), Box::new(combined)))
            }
            _ => Ok(left),
        }
    }

    fn parse_ternary(&mut self) -> PResult<Expr> {
        let cond = self.parse_logic_or()?;
        if self.match_tok(&Tok::Question) {
            // then/else arms parse at assignment level, per C grammar.
            let then_expr = self.parse_assignment()?;
            self.eat(&Tok::Colon)?;
            let else_expr = self.parse_assignment()?;
            Ok(Expr::Ternary {
                cond: Box::new(cond),
                then_expr: Box::new(then_expr),
                else_expr: Box::new(else_expr),
            })
        } else {
            Ok(cond)
        }
    }

    fn parse_logic_or(&mut self) -> PResult<Expr> {
        let mut left = self.parse_logic_and()?;
        while self.check(&Tok::OrOr) {
            self.advance();
            let right = self.parse_logic_and()?;
            left = Expr::Binary(BinOp::Or, Box::new(left), Box::new(right));
        }
        Ok(left)
    }

    fn parse_logic_and(&mut self) -> PResult<Expr> {
        let mut left = self.parse_equality()?;
        while self.check(&Tok::AndAnd) {
            self.advance();
            let right = self.parse_equality()?;
            left = Expr::Binary(BinOp::And, Box::new(left), Box::new(right));
        }
        Ok(left)
    }

    fn parse_equality(&mut self) -> PResult<Expr> {
        let mut left = self.parse_relational()?;
        loop {
            let op = match self.peek() {
                Tok::Eq => BinOp::Eq,
                Tok::Ne => BinOp::Ne,
                _ => break,
            };
            self.advance();
            let right = self.parse_relational()?;
            left = Expr::Binary(op, Box::new(left), Box::new(right));
        }
        Ok(left)
    }

    fn parse_relational(&mut self) -> PResult<Expr> {
        let mut left = self.parse_additive()?;
        loop {
            let op = match self.peek() {
                Tok::Lt => BinOp::Lt,
                Tok::Gt => BinOp::Gt,
                Tok::Le => BinOp::Le,
                Tok::Ge => BinOp::Ge,
                _ => break,
            };
            self.advance();
            let right = self.parse_additive()?;
            left = Expr::Binary(op, Box::new(left), Box::new(right));
        }
        Ok(left)
    }

    fn parse_additive(&mut self) -> PResult<Expr> {
        let mut left = self.parse_multiplicative()?;
        loop {
            let op = match self.peek() {
                Tok::Plus => BinOp::Add,
                Tok::Minus => BinOp::Sub,
                _ => break,
            };
            self.advance();
            let right = self.parse_multiplicative()?;
            left = Expr::Binary(op, Box::new(left), Box::new(right));
        }
        Ok(left)
    }

    fn parse_multiplicative(&mut self) -> PResult<Expr> {
        let mut left = self.parse_unary()?;
        loop {
            let op = match self.peek() {
                Tok::Star => BinOp::Mul,
                Tok::Slash => BinOp::Div,
                Tok::Percent => BinOp::Mod,
                _ => break,
            };
            self.advance();
            let right = self.parse_unary()?;
            left = Expr::Binary(op, Box::new(left), Box::new(right));
        }
        Ok(left)
    }

    fn parse_unary(&mut self) -> PResult<Expr> {
        match self.peek() {
            Tok::Minus => {
                self.advance();
                Ok(Expr::Unary(UnOp::Neg, Box::new(self.parse_unary()?)))
            }
            Tok::Not => {
                self.advance();
                Ok(Expr::Unary(UnOp::Not, Box::new(self.parse_unary()?)))
            }
            Tok::Amp => {
                self.advance();
                Ok(Expr::Unary(UnOp::AddrOf, Box::new(self.parse_unary()?)))
            }
            Tok::Star => {
                self.advance();
                Ok(Expr::Unary(UnOp::Deref, Box::new(self.parse_unary()?)))
            }
            Tok::PlusPlus => {
                self.advance();
                let e = self.parse_unary()?;
                Ok(Expr::IncDec { target: Box::new(e), delta: 1, prefix: true })
            }
            Tok::MinusMinus => {
                self.advance();
                let e = self.parse_unary()?;
                Ok(Expr::IncDec { target: Box::new(e), delta: -1, prefix: true })
            }
            Tok::KwSizeof => {
                self.advance();
                // sizeof(type) | sizeof(expr) | sizeof expr. We keep the
                // operand expression (if any) so the interpreter can compute a
                // synthetic size; sizeof(type) carries no expr (None).
                let operand: Option<Box<Expr>> = if self.check(&Tok::LParen) {
                    self.advance();
                    let op = if self.is_type_start() {
                        self.parse_type()?;
                        None
                    } else {
                        Some(Box::new(self.parse_expr()?))
                    };
                    self.eat(&Tok::RParen)?;
                    op
                } else {
                    // sizeof <unary-expr>, e.g. `sizeof *node`.
                    Some(Box::new(self.parse_unary()?))
                };
                Ok(Expr::Sizeof(operand))
            }
            _ => self.parse_postfix(),
        }
    }

    fn parse_postfix(&mut self) -> PResult<Expr> {
        let mut expr = self.parse_primary()?;
        loop {
            match self.peek() {
                Tok::LBracket => {
                    self.advance();
                    let idx = self.parse_expr()?;
                    self.eat(&Tok::RBracket)?;
                    expr = Expr::Index(Box::new(expr), Box::new(idx));
                }
                Tok::Dot => {
                    self.advance();
                    let field = self.expect_ident()?;
                    expr = Expr::Member { base: Box::new(expr), field, arrow: false };
                }
                Tok::Arrow => {
                    self.advance();
                    let field = self.expect_ident()?;
                    expr = Expr::Member { base: Box::new(expr), field, arrow: true };
                }
                Tok::PlusPlus => {
                    self.advance();
                    expr = Expr::IncDec { target: Box::new(expr), delta: 1, prefix: false };
                }
                Tok::MinusMinus => {
                    self.advance();
                    expr = Expr::IncDec { target: Box::new(expr), delta: -1, prefix: false };
                }
                _ => break,
            }
        }
        Ok(expr)
    }

    fn parse_primary(&mut self) -> PResult<Expr> {
        match self.peek().clone() {
            Tok::Int(n) => {
                self.advance();
                Ok(Expr::IntLit(n))
            }
            Tok::Float(f) => {
                self.advance();
                Ok(Expr::FloatLit(f))
            }
            Tok::Char(c) => {
                self.advance();
                Ok(Expr::CharLit(c))
            }
            Tok::Str(s) => {
                self.advance();
                Ok(Expr::StrLit(s))
            }
            Tok::LParen => {
                self.advance();
                let e = self.parse_expr()?;
                self.eat(&Tok::RParen)?;
                Ok(e)
            }
            Tok::Ident(name) if name == "NULL" => {
                self.advance();
                Ok(Expr::Null)
            }
            Tok::Ident(name) => {
                self.advance();
                if self.check(&Tok::LParen) {
                    self.advance();
                    let mut args = Vec::new();
                    if !self.check(&Tok::RParen) {
                        loop {
                            args.push(self.parse_expr()?);
                            if !self.match_tok(&Tok::Comma) {
                                break;
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    self.eat(&Tok::RParen)?;
                    Ok(Expr::Call(name, args))
                } else {
                    Ok(Expr::Ident(name))
                }
            }
            other => Err(ParseError {
                message: format!("unexpected token in expression: {:?}", other),
                line: self.line(),
            }),
        }
    }
}

//! Serializable execution-trace model.
//!
//! This mirrors the frontend's `frontend/public/src/components/visualization/
//! trace.ts` so the JSON produced here deserializes directly into the
//! visualizer. The tagged `Value` / `HeapObject` enums use serde's internal
//! tagging on a `kind` field to match the TypeScript discriminated unions.

use serde::Serialize;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

/// What a pointer points at. A pointer may target a heap object (array/malloc
/// block) or a stack variable slot (e.g. `&x`). `None` on the Ref means null.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
#[serde(tag = "kind")]
pub enum RefTarget {
    /// Points at a heap object, identified by its heap id.
    #[serde(rename = "heap")]
    Heap { id: String },
    /// Points at a stack variable slot (frame id + variable name).
    #[serde(rename = "stack")]
    Stack {
        #[serde(rename = "frameId")]
        frame_id: String,
        name: String,
    },
}

/// A value stored in a variable slot, array cell, or struct field.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
#[serde(tag = "kind")]
pub enum Value {
    /// Inline, copied-by-value scalar (int, char, double, ...).
    #[serde(rename = "primitive")]
    Primitive {
        /// Display text, e.g. "3", "'a'", "3.14".
        display: String,
        #[serde(rename = "typeName", skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
        type_name: Option<String>,
    },
    /// A pointer. `target` is `None` for a null pointer.
    #[serde(rename = "ref")]
    Ref {
        /// What this reference points at (heap object or stack slot), or null.
        target: Option<RefTarget>,
    },
}

impl Value {
    pub fn primitive(display: impl Into<String>, type_name: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Value::Primitive {
            display: display.into(),
            type_name: Some(type_name.into()),
        }
    }

    pub fn reference(target: Option<RefTarget>) -> Self {
        Value::Ref { target }
    }

    /// Convenience: a reference to a heap object by id.
    pub fn heap_ref(id: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Value::Ref {
            target: Some(RefTarget::Heap { id: id.into() }),
        }
    }

    /// Convenience: a reference to a stack variable slot.
    pub fn stack_ref(frame_id: impl Into<String>, name: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Value::Ref {
            target: Some(RefTarget::Stack {
                frame_id: frame_id.into(),
                name: name.into(),
            }),
        }
    }
}

/// A named binding inside a stack frame (local or parameter).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct Variable {
    pub name: String,
    pub value: Value,
    #[serde(rename = "declaredType", skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub declared_type: Option<String>,
}

/// One function activation on the call stack.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct StackFrame {
    pub id: String,
    #[serde(rename = "functionName")]
    pub function_name: String,
    pub variables: Vec<Variable>,
    #[serde(rename = "isActive", skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub is_active: Option<bool>,
}

/// Anything that can live in the heap.
///
/// The `Struct` variant is part of the shared trace contract (used by struct /
/// object visualizations) even though the current C subset only emits arrays.
#[allow(dead_code)]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
#[serde(tag = "kind")]
pub enum HeapObject {
    #[serde(rename = "array")]
    Array {
        id: String,
        #[serde(rename = "elementType", skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
        element_type: Option<String>,
        elements: Vec<Value>,
    },
    #[serde(rename = "struct")]
    Struct {
        id: String,
        #[serde(rename = "typeName")]
        type_name: String,
        fields: Vec<Variable>,
    },
}

/// One snapshot of the program at a single execution step.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct ProgramState {
    pub step: usize,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub line: Option<usize>,
    /// Call-stack depth at this step (1 = top-level `main`). Used by the
    /// frontend debugger to implement step-over / step-out.
    pub depth: usize,
    pub stack: Vec<StackFrame>,
    /// Heap objects keyed by id. BTreeMap keeps a stable, sorted order.
    pub heap: BTreeMap<String, HeapObject>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub note: Option<String>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub stdout: Option<String>,
}

/// The full execution trace: an ordered list of states to scrub through.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct ExecutionTrace {
    pub states: Vec<ProgramState>,
}

    fn lvalue_of(&mut self, expr: &Expr) -> Result<Location, RuntimeError> {

    }

    fn read_ident(&mut self, name: &str) -> Result<RValue, RuntimeError> {
        let frame = self.find_var_frame(name).ok_or(RuntimeError {
            message: format!("use of undeclared variable '{}'", name),
            line: 0,
        })?;
        self.read_location(&Location::Local { frame, name: name.to_string() })
    }

    /// Find the frame index that declares `name`, searching the current frame
    /// only (C has no closures; globals are not modeled here).
    fn find_var_frame(&self, name: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        let top = self.frames.len().checked_sub(1)?;
        if self.frames[top].slots.contains_key(name) {
            Some(top)
        } else {
            None
        }
    }

    // ---- snapshotting -----------------------------------------------------

    /// Stable id for the frame at index `fi` (must match the id used when
    /// building the StackFrame so pointer arrows resolve to the right row).
    fn frame_id(&self, fi: usize) -> String {
        let name = self
            .frames
            .get(fi)
            .map(|f| f.function_name.as_str())
            .unwrap_or("?");
        format!("frame_{}_{}", fi, name)
    }

    /// Convert a pointer slot into a trace Value, resolving its target to a
    /// heap object or a stack variable slot (so the arrow layer can draw it).
    fn pointer_to_value(&self, p: &Option<Location>) -> TValue {
        match p {
            Some(Location::HeapCell { id, .. }) => TValue::heap_ref(id.clone()),
            Some(Location::HeapField { id, .. }) => TValue::heap_ref(id.clone()),
            Some(Location::HeapObj { id }) => TValue::heap_ref(id.clone()),
            Some(Location::Local { frame, name }) => {
                TValue::stack_ref(self.frame_id(*frame), name.clone())
            }
            None => TValue::reference(None),
        }
    }

    fn snapshot(&mut self, line: Option<usize>, note: Option<String>) {
        let step = self.states.len();

        // Build stack frames for the trace.
        let mut stack = Vec::new();
        let top = self.frames.len().saturating_sub(1);
        for (fi, frame) in self.frames.iter().enumerate() {
            let mut variables = Vec::new();
            for vname in &frame.order {
                let slot = &frame.slots[vname];
                let declared = frame.declared.get(vname).map(|t| t.display());
                let tvalue = match slot {
                    Slot::Scalar(s) => TValue::primitive(s.display(), s.type_name()),
                    Slot::Pointer(p) => self.pointer_to_value(p),
                    Slot::ArrayRef { id, .. } => TValue::heap_ref(id.clone()),
                };
                variables.push(TVariable {
                    name: vname.clone(),
                    value: tvalue,
                    declared_type: declared,
                });
            }
            stack.push(StackFrame {
                id: self.frame_id(fi),
                function_name: frame.function_name.clone(),
                variables,
                is_active: Some(fi == top),
            });
        }

        // Build heap objects for the trace.
        let mut heap: BTreeMap<String, HeapObject> = BTreeMap::new();
        for (id, obj) in &self.heap {
            match obj {
                HeapObjectRuntime::Array(arr) => {
                    let elements = arr
                        .cells
                        .iter()
                        .map(|s| TValue::primitive(s.display(), s.type_name()))
                        .collect();
                    heap.insert(
                        id.clone(),
                        HeapObject::Array {
                            id: id.clone(),
                            element_type: Some(base_type_name(&arr.element_type).to_string()),
                            elements,
                        },
                    );
                }
                HeapObjectRuntime::Struct(s) => {
                    let fields = s
                        .fields
                        .iter()
                        .map(|(fname, slot)| {
                            let value = match slot {
                                Slot::Scalar(sc) => TValue::primitive(sc.display(), sc.type_name()),
                                // A pointer field pointing at another heap
                                // struct becomes a heap ref so the frontend
                                // draws the node->node arrow; null -> no arrow.
                                Slot::Pointer(p) => self.pointer_to_value(p),
                                Slot::ArrayRef { id, .. } => TValue::heap_ref(id.clone()),
                            };
                            TVariable {
                                name: fname.clone(),
                                value,
                                declared_type: None,
                            }
                        })
                        .collect();
                    heap.insert(
                        id.clone(),
                        HeapObject::Struct {
                            id: id.clone(),
                            type_name: s.type_name.clone(),
                            fields,
                        },
                    );
                }
            }
        }

        self.states.push(ProgramState {

    match base {
        BaseType::Double | BaseType::Float => Scalar::Double(0.0),
        BaseType::Char => Scalar::Char('\0'),
        _ => Scalar::Int(0),
    }
}

fn coerce_scalar(s: Scalar, base: &BaseType) -> Scalar {
    match base {
        BaseType::Double | BaseType::Float => Scalar::Double(s.as_f64()),
        BaseType::Char => Scalar::Char(char::from_u32((s.as_i64() & 0xff) as u32).unwrap_or('\0')),
        _ => Scalar::Int(s.as_i64()),

}

}

fn base_type_name(base: &BaseType) -> String {
    match base {
        BaseType::Int => "int".into(),
        BaseType::Char => "char".into(),
        BaseType::Double => "double".into(),
        BaseType::Float => "float".into(),
        BaseType::Long => "long".into(),
        BaseType::Void => "void".into(),
        BaseType::Struct(name) => format!("struct {}", name),
    }
}

fn is_malloc_call(e: &Expr) -> bool {
    matches!(e, Expr::Call(name, _) if name == "malloc")
}

/// Pointer-aware equality. A pointer compares equal to NULL/0 iff it is null;
/// two pointers compare equal iff they target the same location.
fn pointers_equal(a: &RValue, b: &RValue) -> bool {
    fn is_nullish(v: &RValue) -> bool {
        match v {
            RValue::Pointer(None) => true,
            RValue::Scalar(s) => s.as_i64() == 0,
            RValue::Void => true,
            _ => false,
        }
    }
    match (a, b) {
        (RValue::Pointer(pa), RValue::Pointer(pb)) => match (pa, pb) {
            (None, None) => true,
            (Some(la), Some(lb)) => locations_equal(la, lb),
            _ => false,
        },
        // One side is a pointer, the other a scalar (typically 0 / NULL).
        (RValue::Pointer(p), other) | (other, RValue::Pointer(p)) => {
            p.is_none() && is_nullish(other)
        }
        _ => false,
    }
}

fn locations_equal(a: &Location, b: &Location) -> bool {
    match (a, b) {
        (Location::HeapObj { id: x }, Location::HeapObj { id: y }) => x == y,
        (Location::HeapField { id: x, field: fx }, Location::HeapField { id: y, field: fy }) => {
            x == y && fx == fy
        }
        (Location::HeapCell { id: x, index: ix }, Location::HeapCell { id: y, index: iy }) => {
            x == y && ix == iy
        }
        (Location::Local { frame: fa, name: na }, Location::Local { frame: fb, name: nb }) => {
            fa == fb && na == nb
        }
        _ => false,
    }
}

fn stmt_line(stmt: &Stmt) -> usize {
    match stmt {
        Stmt::VarDecl { line, .. } => *line,
        Stmt::ExprStmt(_, line) => *line,
        Stmt::If { line, .. } => *line,
        Stmt::While { line, .. } => *line,
        Stmt::For { line, .. } => *line,
        Stmt::Return(_, line) => *line,
        Stmt::Break(line) => *line,
        Stmt::Continue(line) => *line,
        Stmt::Block(_) => 0,
    }
}
